sections.heading: the state, as the last session *left* it
sections.body:
Assessment: This is the most sales-ready artifact in the whole portfolio. Each teardown carries its own post, its own direct message, and its own evidence trail, which means each one is a complete outreach unit for a brand you can name. And yet the thread is twelve days idle and nothing indicates any of them were sent. The prose gate scored badly on the shipping copy, which is probably the real reason it stalled — the analysis is solid, the writing around it is not. That is a much smaller problem than it feels like, because a teardown lands on the strength of the finding, not the sentence.

Handoff written 13d ago — treat its plan as LIKELY, not current. The timeline below shows what moved since.

Do not rebuild:

sections.heading: what needs *you*
sections.dek: The first option is the recommended one; the rest are the real alternatives with the tradeoff each carries.

items.action: Send all three to their named brands this week, as-is
items.why: Recommended. The findings are verified and the brands are real; the writing polish matters far less than the fact that you noticed something about their product. Costs the discomfort of sending prose you scored low.

items.action: Rewrite the shipping copy with a fresh pen before any send
items.why: Fixes a real quality complaint and protects first impressions, but the gate score was on the wrapper, not the analysis, and another rewrite round is the same avoidance shape as everywhere else on this board.

items.action: Publish the teardowns publicly instead of sending them privately
items.why: Builds the proof surface and reaches brands you have not named, but trades a direct reply from a specific buyer for the hope of being found.
No recorded activity in 12 days while the handoff is still active. Park keeps it resumable and quiet; kill hides it for good (ledger-recoverable).

sections.heading: what this *isn't*
sections.body:
The prose gate score recorded here is severe and the pack does not say whether it was ever addressed. The run also happened alongside a concurrent session that renamed a directory mid-flight, so the location and completeness of these files should be confirmed before sending anything.

Session ledgers keep only the last 10 files per session and are pruned at 7 days, so file counts are a floor, not a census. Sweeps persist their own record, so anything already swept is kept.
